channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Turkistan Region Expands Cotton Cultivation with State Support
item.description: Cotton cultivation area in Turkistan region reached 173.6 thousand hectares, a 29.1 thousand hectare increase from last year. The region plans to harvest 556 thousand tons of cotton this year, with 283 thousand tons already collected. State subsidies support farmers with fertilizers, seeds, and pesticides.

item.title: Akmola region leads Kazakhstan in grain harvest, yielding 6.3 million tons
item.description: The Akmola region has secured first place in Kazakhstan's grain harvest, producing 6.3 million tons of grain. Approximately 90% of the harvested grain is third-grade wheat with high baking qualities and protein content. The region increased its sown area by 110.8 hectares compared to last year, with an average yield of 14 centners per hectare.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Slovenia discuss potential joint film production and film days
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Slovenia are exploring opportunities for joint film production and organizing film festivals in each other's countries. The discussions took place during a meeting between Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Minister of Culture, Aibek Dairbekov, and Slovenia's Ambassador to Kyrgyzstan, Alenka Suhadolnik. Both sides expressed interest in professional exchange and developing animated cinema.

item.title: Osh to Construct 'Jashtyk Arena' Sports and Entertainment Complex by 2030
item.description: Osh plans to build a multi-functional sports and entertainment complex named 'Jashtyk Arena' with a capacity of 5,200 spectators. Construction is slated to begin in March 2027 and conclude by March 2030. The facility will include an ice rink, versatile sports halls, and spaces for cultural events and dining.

item.title: President Tokayev Attends International Kazakh Language Society Congress in Astana
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev participated in the 10th Congress of the International Kazakh Language Society in Astana. He emphasized the critical importance of the Kazakh language as a state, political, and national issue. The President acknowledged the society's significant role in strengthening the state language since its founding in 1989.

item.title: Kulubayev Attends CSTO Joint Meeting in Moscow
item.description: Kyrgyz Foreign Minister Jeenbek Kulubayev participated in a joint meeting of the statutory bodies of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) in Moscow. Discussions focused on the military-political situation, regional security challenges, and the organization's activities. Kulubayev emphasized joint efforts against terrorism, drug trafficking, and cyber threats.

item.title: Ukraine and Russia Discuss Large-Scale Prisoner Exchange in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that during the first day of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi involving Ukraine, Russia, and the US, Kyiv and Moscow discussed a potential large-scale prisoner exchange. The issue of prisoner exchange was a primary topic, with the US intending to continue discussions with Russian representatives. Territorial issues were also raised by the Russian delegation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Offers Turkish Investors State Assets Worth $8.3 Billion
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to expand cooperation with Turkish investors through its state enterprise and real estate privatization program. A memorandum signed between Uzbekistan's State Assets Management Agency and Turkey's Foreign Economic Relations Council facilitates informing Turkish companies about assets for sale and attracting foreign capital. Assets valued at over $8.3 billion are planned for privatization in 2026-2027.

item.title: Nearly One-Third of Russia's Refinery Capacity Damaged by Attacks, Reuters Reports
item.description: Approximately one-third of Russia's oil refinery capacity has been taken offline due to Ukrainian attacks, according to Reuters. In the past week, attacks have disrupted operations at 9 out of 35 major Russian refineries. The affected refineries have a combined daily capacity of about 300,000 tons, with an estimated actual reduction of 200,000 tons per day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Stricter Rules for Protecting Fertile Soil Layer
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering new regulations to enhance land protection and state control over land and water resources. The proposed rules mandate measures to prevent soil erosion, salinization, and degradation, requiring developers to preserve and reuse fertile topsoil during construction and mining. The draft also prohibits mixing fertile soil with construction waste.

item.title: Iran President Calls for Afghanistan Rail Link to China
item.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has emphasized the importance of building a rail link between Herat and Mazar-e-Sharif to connect Afghanistan to China's rail network. This project aims to make Afghanistan a key transit route for trade between Iran and China.

item.title: Uralsk Incident: Ex-Police Officer Wounded, Second Former Officer Under Investigation
item.description: An investigation is underway in Uralsk following a knife-wounding incident involving former police officers. One former officer was hospitalized with a penetrating wound. Authorities are examining all versions of the event, including the possible involvement of another ex-officer.

item.title: Tajikistan's Foreign Minister Addresses International Collective Security Forum
item.description: Tajikistan's Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Mukhriddin participated in an international forum on collective security, speaking on "Collective Security in a Multipolar World." He emphasized strengthening international and regional cooperation, improving security mechanisms, and fostering dialogue amid geopolitical realities. The minister highlighted the need for coordinated approaches to counter new challenges and threats.

item.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps Displays New Underground Missile City
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has revealed a new underground missile city for its Aerospace Force. The facility was inspected by Iran's Armed Forces Chief of Staff, Ali Abdollahi. This follows Tehran's announcement of lifting restrictions on missile range, with state television showing a map of potential strikes on European cities and Ukraine.

item.title: US Senator Marco Rubio: No Need for Further Military Strikes on Iran Due to Economic Pressure
item.description: US Senator Marco Rubio stated that Washington sees no need for further extensive military action against Iran due to the severe impact of economic sanctions. His remarks followed a G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris. This comes as Iran reiterates its proposal regarding the Strait of Hormuz, demanding sanctions relief from the US.

item.title: Heavy Snowfall at Otmok Pass Leads to Restrictions on Heavy Vehicle Traffic
item.description: Due to heavy snowfall and slippery road conditions on the Suusamyr-Talas-Taraz highway at Otmok Pass, temporary restrictions have been imposed on all types of heavy cargo vehicles. The Ministry of Transport and Communications stated the measure aims to prevent accidents and ensure public safety.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prioritizes Energy Independence with Atyrau Power Development Plan
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev is prioritizing energy independence and security, leading to a development plan for Atyrau region's electricity sector until 2034. The region faces persistent power outages due to aging infrastructure. Five major projects totaling 1,290 MW are planned by 2030.

item.title: Almaty Teen Sent to Boarding School After Fatal Stabbing; Parents Fined
item.description: A teenager convicted of fatally stabbing a 12-year-old boy in Almaty has been sentenced to one year at a special boarding school. The perpetrator's parents were fined approximately 86,000 tenge. The victim's family considers the decision unjust, arguing the case was not brought to trial and demanding legal changes.

item.title: New Construction Requirements Enforced in Bishkek and Osh
item.description: Explanations are being provided on construction sites in Bishkek and Osh regarding new requirements. The Ministry of Construction has prohibited the sale and advertising of residential and non-residential premises until the "zero cycle" of construction is completed. This applies to projects like "Manas" in Bishkek and "Ene Sai City" in Osh.

item.title: Onion Prices in Tajikistan Surge 60% in a Month Amid Rising Vegetable Costs
item.description: The average price of onions in Tajikistan has increased by 60% in the past month, reaching 4 somoni per kilogram, with some areas selling them for 5-6 somoni. Cabbage, bell peppers, and potatoes have also seen price hikes, while tomatoes and cucumbers have become cheaper. Farmers cite storage and transportation costs for the price increases.

item.title: Kyrgyz University Startup Wins First Place in AI Competition
item.description: A Kyrgyz National Agrarian University startup project called "CowID" won first place at the "InnovTech Startup Challenge 2026". The project uses artificial intelligence and Face ID technology to identify cattle by their muzzle features and detect signs of estrus, helping farmers optimize breeding and farm management. Other university projects also received awards.

item.title: Russia Refuses to Discuss Ceasefire with Ukraine in UAE Talks
item.description: Trilateral talks involving Russia, Ukraine, and the US resumed in Abu Dhabi, with Russia maintaining its refusal to discuss a ceasefire. Kyiv considers ending the war the primary condition for further negotiations. US envoy Jared Kushner stated Washington has constructive proposals for peace, while Ukraine's delegation met with European partners to discuss post-war security architecture.

item.title: Uzbek President Discusses Priority Projects with Saudi Arabian Delegation
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with a Saudi Arabian delegation led by the Minister of Energy. They discussed expanding bilateral cooperation, particularly in green energy, oil and gas, petrochemicals, and mining. The meeting occurred during the UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya.

item.title: Uzbek President Stresses Importance of Expanding Practical Cooperation with Georgia
item.description: During a visit to Turkey, Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Georgian President Mikheil Kavelashvili. They discussed expanding strategic partnership, noting increased contacts between parliaments, ministries, and businesses. Trade turnover and joint ventures are growing, with a digital bank established with Georgian investors.

item.title: Uzbek President Discusses Cooperation Priorities with EBRD Head
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) President Odile Renaud-Basso in Antalya to discuss expanding strategic partnership. Uzbekistan has been the largest recipient of EBRD funds in the region for six years, with a project portfolio exceeding $7 billion. The bank's contribution to the green economy, accounting for 60% of its investments in Uzbekistan, was highly praised. Priorities for the next year include modernizing power grids and developing the agro-food sector.

item.title: Tashkent Airport Temporarily Halts Customs Clearance for New Phones
item.description: Tashkent International Airport has temporarily suspended customs clearance for newly imported mobile devices. The halt is in effect until clarification on issues related to identifying IMEI identifiers and confirming legal import. The Customs Committee stated that increased illegal import attempts and complex schemes involving IMEI cloning have been observed.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Expand Inter-Parliamentary Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan's parliamentary delegation met with South Korea's National Assembly Committee on Culture, Sports, and Tourism to discuss expanding inter-parliamentary cooperation. Key topics included the 'Electronic Parliament' project, digitalization of parliamentary activities, and cooperation in culture, tourism, and sports.

item.title: Parliamentary Inquiry Sent to Director of Technical Regulation Agency
item.description: The Legislative Chamber of Uzbekistan's Oliy Majlis has sent a parliamentary inquiry to the Director of the Technical Regulation Agency regarding the effective organization of state management, digitalization, and the formation of a transparent, corruption-free system in technical regulation.

item.title: Ukraine, Russia, and US Conclude First Day of Peace Talks in Abu Dhabi
item.description: The first day of three-way talks between Ukraine, Russia, and the US on ending the war in Ukraine concluded in Abu Dhabi. The 4.5-hour meeting, with a 40-minute break, yielded no official results yet. A source close to the Ukrainian delegation reported an agreement for a large-scale prisoner exchange soon.

item.title: Iran Accuses France of Blaming Others for Own Incompetence
item.description: Iran's foreign minister, Seyed Abbas Araghchi, accused French officials of deflecting blame for domestic failures onto Iran regarding a cyberattack. He stated on X that France covers up its shortcomings by blaming others and is unable to manage domestic affairs or protests. Iran's Foreign Ministry called French allegations baseless.

item.title: Uzbekistan Achieves Record Cotton Harvest Exceeding 5 Million Tons
item.description: Uzbekistan has achieved a historic cotton harvest, surpassing 5 million tons for the first time in the New Uzbekistan era. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated farmers, highlighting the transformation of the agricultural sector. This success reflects a shift towards intensive development, innovation, and farmer economic interest.

item.title: Uzbekistan President meets with Green Climate Fund Executive Director
item.description: During the COP31 summit in Antalya, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Mafalda Duarte, Executive Director of the Green Climate Fund. Discussions focused on expanding cooperation in climate change adaptation and attracting climate finance. The fund's partnership with Uzbekistan has grown, with joint projects exceeding $200 million.

item.title: China and Central Asia Expand Air Connectivity to Boost Trade and Tourism
item.description: China and Central Asian aviation officials met in Tashkent to enhance existing agreements and plan expansions. Kazakhstan will increase weekly flights to 180 and add new routes, while Uzbekistan will raise its flights to China to 114. Air Astana and China Southern Airlines formed a strategic partnership.

item.title: Turkmenistan President Oversees Agricultural Progress and Infrastructure Development
item.description: President Serdar Berdimuhamedow held a working meeting focusing on agricultural tasks and regional development. He emphasized timely completion of cotton harvesting and wheat sowing, proper crop care, and maximizing harvests. The president also stressed the importance of quality construction of planned facilities and ensuring the proper functioning of heating systems in educational, cultural, and residential buildings.

item.title: Kazakh President Travels to Moscow for CSTO Collective Security Council Meeting
item.description: The President of Kazakhstan has traveled to Moscow to participate in a meeting of the CSTO Collective Security Council. The meeting is expected to address regional security issues and cooperation among member states.

item.title: Turkmenistan's National Leader Meets with Renaissance Holding Chairman in Turkey
item.description: Turkmenistan's National Leader, Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow, met with Erman Ilıcak, Chairman of Renaissance Holding, during his working visit to Turkey. Ilıcak expressed gratitude for the opportunity and highlighted Turkish business groups' interest in developing mutually beneficial relations with Turkmenistan. They discussed expanding trade and economic ties.

item.title: Sadyr Japarov Applies to Run for Kyrgyzstan Presidency Again in 2027 Election
item.description: Sadyr Japarov has submitted an application to run for president of Kyrgyzstan in the upcoming election scheduled for January 27, 2027. He aims to secure a second term in office. Currently, six individuals have declared their candidacy for the presidency.

item.title: Iran Denies US Claims of Talks, States Hormuz Strait Closure Condition
item.description: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, has called US claims of ongoing negotiations with Tehran a "complete lie." He stated that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until Iran's seven announced conditions are met. Rezaei asserted that US claims aim to ease economic pressure and lower oil prices, and that Iran awaits a clear response to its conditions.

item.title: Afghan UN Envoy: Denying Girls Education is Betrayal and Blow to Future
item.description: Afghanistan's UN Representative Nasir Ahmad Faiq stated that denying girls education and restricting boys' access to modern sciences is a betrayal of a generation and harmful to Afghanistan's future. He emphasized education as a human right crucial for progress and fighting poverty.

item.title: Outdated Standards Hinder Uzbekistan's WTO Accession, Deputies Raise Concerns
item.description: Uzbekistan's path to joining the World Trade Organization is being obstructed by outdated national standards, according to lawmakers. A parliamentary inquiry has been sent to the head of the "Uzstandard" Agency, highlighting issues with technical regulation, digitalization, and corruption risks. Approximately half of Uzbekistan's 33,000 active standards are reportedly obsolete or do not meet international requirements.
